summary.text: A 39-year-old woman with a history of sickle cell disease presented with increased left flank swelling for the past 2 years, first noticed many years ago as a 1 cm soft, painless mass and approximately 10 cm on presentation, and dull lower back pain beginning six months prior to presentation. She reported no recent fevers or weight change. She immigrated from Nigeria one year ago, has no known history of or exposure to TB and received the BCG vaccine as a child.

Examination showed a well-demarcated 10 cm × 16 cm fluctuant area of the back without erythema, icteric sclera and enlarged cervical lymph nodes, with an unremarkable cardiopulmonary, abdominal and neurologic examination. Rapid HIV testing was negative, blood cultures remained sterile, and total bilirubin was 148.8 μmol/L. CT and follow-up MRI showed L4-L5 diskitis and osteomyelitis with abscesses extending into the epidural space; Gram stain and acid-fast staining were negative for any organisms.

A tuberculous cold abscess was high on the differential and isoniazid, rifampin, pyrazinamide and ethambutol were empirically started. Orthopedic and neurosurgery specialists were consulted for surgical drainage, but the patient and neurosurgeons were initially reluctant to perform the procedure and she was discharged on anti-TB medications and pyridoxine. At follow-up at a local TB clinic she had right upper quadrant pain and elevated transaminases; all medications were stopped and rifampin and ethambutol were restarted a week later.

Four weeks from presentation, cultures from drained abscess revealed Mycobacterium tuberculosis and the diagnosis was confirmed. At this time she was reevaluated by neurosurgery and underwent paraspinal abscess drainage through paravertebral muscles, and was briefly treated with moxifloxacin following the procedure. At her last clinic visit, six months into her treatment course, she was on isoniazid, rifampin and pyridoxine without any complaints.
